To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the best conditions for producing adsorbent from corn cobs or mango kernels using H 3 PO4 impregnation method are by soaking the sample for 2-3 hours and using 1:1 ratio of sample to acid.
the activated carbon from mango kernels and corncobs have a high adsorption capacity of copper and nickel, with a 3 hour soaking time.

the best conditions for the production of activated carbon are the use of 85% H3PO4 as an activating agent, with soaking time at 3 hours for the production of KAC (Kernel activated carbon) and CAC(Corn activated carbon), and 2 hours for KAC and 3 hours for CAC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of activated carbon from mango kernels and corncobs using H 3 PO4 activation and mediated by hydrothermal treatment and its application in heavy metals removal from wastewater.
the production and analysis of activated carbon from Mango Kernel and Corn Cob.
the production and characterization of activated carbons from mango kernels and corncobs, and their use as a metal adsorbent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both mango kernel and corn cobs can be used to produce activated carbon, and that the activated carbon produced is a good adsorption material for heavy metals.
the activated carbon produced by H 3 PO4 impregnation and mediated hydrothermal process is an efficient adsorbent of heavy metals.
the best activated carbon produced from hydrothermal treatment of mango kernels and corn cob is the 2 HR and the 3 HR samples, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
both CAC and CAC are good adsorbents of Copper and Nickel.
both CAC and KC are good adsorbents for Copper, Nickel, and Lead.
the adsorption of Cu and Ni by the activated carbon of mango kernels and corn cob is better than the adsorption of Pb by activated carbon of mango kernel and corn cob.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the adsorption capacity of the samples is directly proportional to residence time, and the best conditions for adsorptive capacity are obtained by soaking for 2 hours for KAC and CAC.
the adsorption of heavy metal is affected by both the surface morphology and the surface functional group.
we were able to produce activated carbon from mango kernels and corncobs using H 3 PO4 activation and hydrothermal treatment.
